conventions.convention: Use the fixed ordered Euclidean orthonormal basis; Du has entries ∂j ui. For time-dependent fields, Du, gradients and divergence are spatial derivatives at fixed time. Dt f = ∂t f + Dx f(u), componentwise for vector fields.

A motion is jointly C² on I × O, with O open containing the reference region's closure, injective regular time slices, and positive Jacobian on I × B. Velocity is defined on the open spacetime image of I × O. Boundary regularity is an additional hypothesis.

The Lebesgue transport and localization results assume countable choice. Transport needs C¹ field data on an open neighborhood of the closed sweep and uses local compact time cylinders; it imposes no boundary smoothness on B.

Traction is σν with the outward normal, and matrix divergence is the row divergence gi = Σj ∂j σij. Momentum localization additionally assumes continuity equation (K) and integral balance (L) on admissible current C¹ domains.
Linear strain is (Dξ + Dξᵀ)/2; elastic coefficients satisfy μ > 0 and λ + 2μ/3 > 0. Energy is W(e) = λ(tr e)²/2 + μ tr(e²).

Weak/entropy fields and initial data are bounded Borel functions under countable choice. The displayed spacetime integral denotes one λ₂ integral. Tests are compactly supported C¹ functions up to t = 0 with possibly nonzero initial trace. Entropy inequality (E) has nonnegative integrated residual.
Chain indices are cyclic modulo N, N ≥ 2; a > 0 and c > 0. The scaled norm is a Σj zj², while the definition's unscaled energy differs from the later energy Ea by a factor a.
Sine modes start at n = 1; bn(F) = (2/L) ∫₀ᴸ F(x) sin(nπx/L) dx. These are ordinary Riemann integrals. The continuous odd extension is 2L-periodic and requires both endpoint values to vanish.

The continuum-limit closed-time regularity means restriction from an open neighborhood; chain solutions are restrictions of solutions on an open time interval. At T = 0 uniqueness concerns the restricted state (q, q′), so initial derivatives remain defined.

load_bearing.statement: Under countable choice, for the stated motion ψ and C¹ field f on an open neighborhood of its closed sweep, F(t) = ∫ψt(B) f(t,x) dx is differentiable on J₀ and F′(t) = ∫ψt(B) (∂t f + div(fw))(t,x) dx. The formula also holds componentwise.

A motion χ:I × O → R³ is C², each χt is injective with invertible spatial derivative, O contains the reference region's closure, and det DXχt > 0 on I × B. Its spatial velocity satisfies u(t,χ(t,X)) = ∂tχ(t,X).
For n ≥ 1, entries of A:I → Mn(R) differentiable at t₀, and A(t) invertible for every t ∈ I, (det A)′(t₀) = det A(t₀) tr(A(t₀)⁻¹A′(t₀)).

Assume countable choice. If H is continuous on open W ⊆ R³ and its defined signed integrals vanish on a family of nonempty open subsets containing, around each point, a member inside every neighborhood, then H = 0 on W.

Under the stated motion, field regularity, countable choice, continuity equation (K), and integral momentum balance (L) on every admissible material-subregion/current-C¹-domain pair, ρ Dt u = ρ b + g on the current interior, where gi = Σj ∂j σij.

A continuous traction t:O × S² → R³, balanced with a bounded continuous volume field g on every stated finite-piecewise-C¹ test domain compactly inside O, has a unique continuous representing matrix σ(y), with columns t(y,ei), and t(y,−n) = −t(y,n).

For odd 2L-periodic C⁵ displacement data F and C⁴ velocity data G, L,c > 0, the stated sine series is C², solves the fixed-end wave problem with those data, has the stated C² uniqueness property, and its N-mode tail is at most 2(2L⁵M₅/π⁵ + 2L⁵M₄/(cπ⁵))(N+1)⁻⁴.

For the stated smooth periodic wave solution and sampled cyclic-chain data, the chain solution exists uniquely; with C = c²√L M/12, ||e(t)||a ≤ Ca²t²/2, ||e′(t)||a ≤ Ca²t, maxj |ej(t)| ≤ Ca³ᐟ²t²/2, and interpolation error is at most maxj |ej(t)| + M₂a²/8 on [0,T].

Under countable choice, the decreasing Riemann shock has speed (uL+uR)/2 and is a weak and entropy solution. Its Kružkov integrated interface coefficient is −(k−uL)(k−uR) inside [uR,uL] and zero outside. The increasing rarefaction is a continuous weak and entropy solution, with entropy equality for the stated pairs.

concerns.concern: The final Remark says: “If a body couple density or a surface couple field is present, the balance (B) must be modified and the reversed-normal conclusion can fail for the full traction”. This is unsupported by the theorem or proof. A couple modifies angular balance; the stated pure-force balance (B), when retained, still forces the reversed-normal identity by the thin-box argument irrespective of angular balance. “Full traction” has no additional definition here. The main theorem's conditional proof is sound, but this extra caveat needs justification or correction.

The Statement requires p:(0,∞) → R to be “the restriction of a C¹ map on an open neighbourhood of the rectangle”. No rectangle is defined at this point, and p has a one-dimensional density domain. The proof only needs the ordinary C¹ pressure law of def-cm-fluid-constitutive-models. The material-loop mixed derivative is supplied correctly in step 1.1; the defect is the malformed pressure-law hypothesis.

The last Remark says the “longitudinal and transverse speeds ... require μ>0 and λ+2μ>0 respectively”. These conditions are reversed: the displayed formulas give cL²=(λ+2μ)/ρ₀ and cT²=μ/ρ₀. The Statement and proof use the correct formulas.

Clause (b) describes c²κ⁴a²/12 as “an explicit fourth-order error in the spacing”. For fixed κ the bound is second order in spacing a and fourth order in wave number κ. The formula and proof are correct.

Step 1.2 says “Applying [F1] in t to t↦w(t,x) gives ∂tw(t,x)=z(t,x)”. F1 applies to a sequence, not the already defined limit w. The immediate completion is to apply it to t↦∂xu_k(t,x), whose derivatives ∂t∂xu_k converge uniformly to z and whose values converge to w.

The Facts' Given line calls J₀ compactly contained and Σ compact, whereas the Statement only requires closure(J₀) ⊆ I and permits unbounded J₀. Step 1.1 and the Remarks explicitly use local compact cylinders and correctly cover that broader Statement. The Given line should agree with that local proof.

alerts.finding: The other-batch page cm15-scattering-and-impulse-model-boundaries-examples summarizes ex-cm15-impact-check by saying “the elastic case exchanges the velocities”. With its masses 2 and 6 kg and incoming velocities 3n and −n, the item correctly computes outgoing velocities −3n and +n in Verification 2.1. These reverse each velocity; they do not exchange the incoming values. The defect is in the page summary, not the item's computation.

F2 restates thm-cm-local-mass-balance as an equivalence between conservation and the local equation on the current interior, then acknowledges that the cited converse uses an open neighborhood of the sweep. The supplier states two implications with different domain hypotheses, rather than that exact equivalence. The consumer's actual converse in Proof 1.2 retains the stronger neighborhood hypothesis and is faithful; F2's initial equivalence wording is overcompressed.
